title: Coleslaw
subtitle: Crisp white cabbage and carrot in a creamy mustard dressing
excerpt: White cabbage and carrots finely shredded and dressed in a creamy mayonnaise and wholegrain mustard dressing. Properly made coleslaw is crunchy, not soggy. Rest it for 30 minutes before serving.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coleslaw derives from the Dutch 'koolsla' (cabbage salad) and was brought to North America by Dutch settlers. The British version uses a mayonnaise-based dressing rather than a vinaigrette, and is a standard accompaniment to barbecued meat, pulled pork, and fish and chips. Salting the cabbage before dressing it draws out excess water and prevents the coleslaw from becoming watery as it stands.

content.text: Salt the shredded cabbage and leave it for 15 minutes before squeezing out the excess liquid. This one step prevents watery coleslaw. Shred the cabbage as finely as possible for the best texture: use a mandoline or the fine slicer attachment of a food processor if available.
Put the shredded cabbage in a large colander. Sprinkle with the salt and toss. Leave for 15 minutes. Squeeze handfuls firmly to expel as much liquid as possible. Transfer to a large bowl.
Add the grated carrot and sliced onion to the bowl. Mix the mayonnaise, wholegrain mustard, cider vinegar, and sugar in a small bowl until combined.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss thoroughly so every strand is coated. Taste and adjust seasoning. Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes before serving: the flavours deepen as it sits.
